title: Bread made from wheat or cracked wheat, reduced calorie and/or high fiber

content.title: About
content.content: Bread made from whole wheat or cracked wheat is a whole‑grain loaf prepared with flour from intact wheat kernels or with coarse wheat groats. The reduced‑calorie version contains less fat and sugar, while the high‑fiber version is enriched with additional dietary fiber, making it more filling and beneficial for digestion.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain bread retains the bran and germ, giving it more nutrients than white bread.
Cracked wheat (also known as bulgur) has been a staple in traditional diets of many cultures, including ancient Roman and medieval cuisines.
High‑fiber bread can help stabilize blood sugar levels.
Reduced‑calorie formulations often use alternative sweeteners and lower fat content to cut calories.
Fiber increases satiety, helping with weight management.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy bowel movements, promotes regularity, and feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Lower calorie content
items.content: Fewer calories aid in maintaining an energy balance during weight loss.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole wheat provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The bread supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and low saturated fat content help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may experience serious reactions to this bread.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Because it is made from wheat, the bread is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Some varieties may contain higher salt; individuals with hypertension should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread can be enjoyed on its own, used for sandwiches, toasted for breakfast, served alongside soups, or as a base for open‑face toppings. Toasting enhances flavor and creates a pleasant crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze the bread and allow it to thaw at room temperature before use.
